svg.text: Idea 2 as the literature check read it: PVSE with masked sub-space training in place of the K attention heads
Two readings of “masked sub-space”. In both, the masked caption decoder is the signal that assigns a caption (a reading) to one of K sub-spaces.
PVSE (Song and Soleymani, CVPR 2019): what is replaced
embeddings that agrees most carries the loss
+ a diversity loss that keeps the K apart
retrieval: max over the K × K pairs
↓ replaced by: K sub-spaces that a masked caption decoder assigns readings to ↓
Reading (a): K sub-spaces of the embedding dimensions (masks on the 512-d pooled embedding)
each sub-embedding conditions the decoder in turn
the caption goes to the sub-space whose
contrastive loss on the assigned pair
retrieval: max over k of the sub-space similarities
control the check names: one vector of the same total size, and random fixed masks
(Li and Jurafsky: multi-sense gains can come from capacity alone)
Reading (b): K embeddings, each from a different masked view of the image
each view conditions the decoder in turn
the reading goes to the view
contrastive loss per view with its assigned caption
(needed: views trained by pixels alone collapse,
retrieval: max over the K views
risk the check names: a view encodes where in the image, not which reading;
comparator: attentive views with multi-positive InfoNCE (A-CLIP style)

Shared knob in both readings: the masking ratio. DML (NeurIPS 2022): a fully masked caption decoder with Hungarian assignment keeps 29 of 64 codes in use; partial or no masking keeps 5 or 6. Shared risk: the K readings collapse into one.
